meta.title: The potential adverse effects of hypodermic glucagon-like peptide -1 receptor agonist on patients with type 2 diabetes: A population-based study.
meta.abstract:
Background

Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), a class of injectable antidiabetic drugs, have shown significant efficacies in improving glycemic and weight control in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D). However, the long-term safety of GLP-1 RAs remains insufficiently studied. This study aimed to provide real-world evidence on potential adverse outcomes associated with GLP-1 RAs use in T2D patients without major chronic diseases including impaired cardiac or renal function.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study involving 7746 T2D patients on GLP-1 RAs in Shenzhen, China. They were compared with 124 371 metformin-only users and 36 146 insulin-only users, forming two therapy control groups. GLP-1 RAs users were also further 1:2 paired with the control groups. Competing risk survival analyses were conducted to assess the incidence risks, presenting subdistributional hazard ratios (sHRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for various adverse outcomes associated with GLP-1 RAs use.

Results

Compared with metformin-only users, GLP-1 RAs use was associated with increased risks of various adverse outcomes (sHRs with 95% CIs), including pancreatitis (2.01, 1.24-3.24), acute nephritis (3.20, 2.17-4.70), kidney failure (3.73, 2.74-5.08), thyroid cancer (2.25, 1.23-4.10), and thyroid dysfunction (1.27, 1.00-1.63), respectively; Similar results were also found when compared with insulin-only users. Importantly, long-term (≥12 months) GLP-1 RAs use may further elevate the incidence risks of pancreatitis, acute nephritis, thyroid cancer, and thyroid dysfunction.

Conclusion

Compared with traditional T2D treatments, GLP-1 RAs use may be associated with increased risks of various adverse outcomes in a Chinese population. Cautions were strongly warranted in the use of GLP-1 RAs. Further validation is crucial across diverse populations.

domains.name: Confounding
domains.direction_justification: GLP-1 RA users had higher baseline proportions of overweight/obesity (BMI 25-29.9: 30.51% vs 20.57% in insulin, 29.50% in metformin; BMI 30-39.9: 13.21% vs 3.04% in insulin, 4.87% in metformin) and higher socioeconomic status (Citizen health insurance: 75.60% vs 59.60% in insulin, 54.96% in metformin; Undergraduate+: 26.07% vs 15.65% in insulin, 11.94% in metformin in Table 3S). Key clinical confounders including baseline disease duration, eGFR, and glycemic control (HbA1c missing in 90.52% to 91.79%) were unmeasured or unadjusted, pushing risk estimates away from the null.

domains.name: Selection of participants into the study
domains.direction_justification: Conditioning cohort membership on maintaining predominant monotherapy throughout the follow-up period (<6 months of other antidiabetic drugs) introduces selection bias and immortal/continuation bias, enriching the cohort for persistent users or distinct clinical trajectories.

findings.title: Post-baseline criteria in cohort definition
findings.mechanism: Requiring patients to maintain predominant use of GLP-1 RA, insulin, or metformin from baseline to the end of follow-up (<6 months switch/add-on) conditions on post-baseline behavior.
evidence: Cohort restricted to patients whose accumulative prescription primarily consisted of one drug class from baseline to last follow-up date
Only 7,746 GLP-1 RA users were retained out of 380,370 eligible baseline patients

domains.name: Post-exposure interventions
domains.direction_justification: The statistical modeling defined the occurrence of acute symptoms (diarrhea/emesis, tetter, acne, dizziness, arrhythmia) as competing risk events that censor or terminate follow-up, differentially altering the risk set between GLP-1 RA users and standard treatment controls.

findings.title: Non-standard competing risk definitions
findings.mechanism: Treating mild or transient side effects as competing fatal events distorts subdistribution hazard estimates for hard clinical outcomes.
evidence: Methods Section 2.3: 'potential competing events were systematically defined as a binomial variable, activated by any incidence of specific acute symptoms, including diarrhea/emesis, dermatitis tetter, acne, dizziness, arrhythmia, etc.'

domains.name: Missing data
domains.direction_justification: Over 90% of participants had missing HbA1c data (90.52% in GLP-1 RA, 91.79% in insulin, 90.45% in metformin), ~33% had missing fasting glucose, and ~33% had missing BMI, yet PSM was performed by matching missing indicator categories.

findings.title: Severe missingness in critical prognostic markers
findings.mechanism: Matching on 'unspecified' missing categories allows patients with high disease severity/glycemia to be matched to patients with low severity simply because their values were missing in the health records.
evidence: HbA1c missing rates: 90.52% in GLP-1 RAs, 91.79% in insulin-only, 90.45% in metformin-only (Table 3S note)
Fasting plasma glucose missing rates: 32.95% in GLP-1 RAs, 32.66% in insulin-only, 24.13% in metformin-only (Table 3S note)
BMI missing in 33.81% of matched GLP-1 RA vs 36.08% in insulin group (Table 1)

domains.name: Measurement of the outcome
domains.direction_justification: Patients receiving novel injectable therapies undergo greater clinical monitoring, frequent laboratory screening, and imaging compared to patients on stable oral metformin monotherapy, inflating the detection of incidental conditions such as thyroid nodules/cancer, acute nephritis, or leukemia.

findings.title: Surveillance / Detection bias in EHR data
findings.mechanism: Outcomes were identified via ICD-10 and free-text regular expressions from routine outpatient/inpatient records without adjudication. Increased surveillance in GLP-1 RA users increases diagnosis rates of subclinical disease.
evidence: Thyroid cancer sHR 2.25 (95% CI: 1.23-4.10) for <12 months and 3.43 (95% CI: 1.30-9.03) for >=12 months vs metformin (Figure 3)
Leukemia sHR 15.09 (95% CI: 4.65-48.98) after >=12 months vs metformin (Figure 3) and sHR 6.88 (95% CI: 2.06-22.94) vs insulin (Figure 2)
Renal failure sHR 3.73 (95% CI: 2.74-5.08) vs metformin (Figure 3)

domains.name: Selection of the reported result
domains.direction_justification: Dozens of outcomes across multiple organ systems and sub-agents were analyzed across short-term (<12m) and long-term (>=12m) subgroups without pre-specified protocol registration or formal multiple testing correction, increasing the likelihood of reporting extreme effect estimates.

findings.title: Multiple testing and outcome dredging without multiplicity correction
findings.mechanism: Evaluating multiple non-prespecified adverse events (including acute nephritis, follicular cysts, acne, leukemia, liver cirrhosis, intestinal obstruction) across multiple drug-specific subgroups inflates false-positive findings.
evidence: Outcomes covered 6 disease systems across outpatient and inpatient records (Table 2S)
Leukemia showed sHR 15.09 (95% CI: 4.65-48.98) after >=12 months, acknowledged by authors as potential random bias from low case counts (Discussion Section 4)

overall.summary: This retrospective observational cohort study exhibits very high risk of bias across multiple critical ROBINS-E domains. Major threats include massive missing data for primary prognostic variables (>90% missing HbA1c, >30% missing glucose and BMI), failure of propensity score matching by treating missingness as an explicit matching category, substantial surveillance/detection bias favoring detection of incidental outcomes in GLP-1 RA users, and biologically implausible effect sizes (e.g., leukemia sHR 15.09) driven by low event numbers and unadjusted multiple testing. Consequently, the study findings do not support causal inferences regarding GLP-1 RA adverse effects.

unresolvable_without_more_data: Raw event counts and person-years per group for each individual adverse event to compute absolute risk differences and incidence rates.
Complete baseline clinical variables (measured HbA1c, eGFR/creatinine, baseline diabetes duration, microvascular complication history, smoking status) without high rates of missingness.
Information on outpatient encounter frequency and diagnostic test ordering rates per group to evaluate and adjust for surveillance/detection bias.

baseline_comparability.summary: Baseline imbalances in the unmatched cohort showed GLP-1 RA users were younger, had markedly higher rates of obesity (BMI >=30: 13.21% vs 3.04-4.87%), and substantially higher insurance coverage (75.60% vs 54.96-59.60%). Although demographic matching achieved balance on measured covariates, extreme missingness in glycemic variables (>90% for HbA1c) and unmeasured diabetes duration likely pushed effect estimates away from the null via surveillance bias and residual confounding.

time_related_biases.summary: The study defines exposure groups based on predominant treatment across total follow-up, introducing conditioning on future time and immortal time bias. Furthermore, the absence of a lag period combined with a mean follow-up under 2 years leads to severe detection bias and reverse causation for latent oncologic and chronic endpoints.
